title: What Counts as the Premium Collected on a Re-Rating
content:
What counts as the premium collected on a policy of the Travel Protection Plans, when the certificate is
re-rated, is read from the policy's own premium record where that record is able to answer, and from the policy
record itself where it is not.

## The three readings

| What the premium record carries | The premium the record shows collected |
|---|---|
| A line returned on the policy, and a base premium line | The lines charged and the re-ratings raised, less the lines returned, the policy fee excepted |
| A base premium line and no line returned | The lines charged and the re-ratings raised, the policy fee excepted |
| Neither of those | The figure the policy record shows paid |

In the first two readings the issue fee charged on the certificate is taken out of the total, the fee being no
part of what was collected for the risk.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A premium record carrying charges of 680.00, of which 15.00 is the policy fee, a re-rating of 45.00 and a line
returned of 120.00 falls under the first reading, and the premium collected is 590.00. The same record without
the returned line falls under the second, and the premium collected is 710.00. A record carrying no base premium
line at all falls under the third, and the premium collected is whatever figure the policy record shows paid.
The figures are hypothetical.
